replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the facts here are not really in dispute, and the money follows from them.

What happened. On 14 July an LTA water-main repair closed Braddell Road (towards Serangoon, between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd) from 05:30 to 12:00 — the very stretch the booked optimal route uses. The driver diverted via the CTE, which is one of the diversions the advisory itself signs. The GPS trace is complete and unimpaired for policy purposes (175 fixes at the 10-second interval, coverage 100%, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s), so the excess is measured on it as POL-RD-01 requires: 11.18 km trace distance against the 8.2 km booked optimal, an excess of 2.98 km (36.3%).

Driver's exoneration — accepted in full. POL-RD-03 is satisfied: the advisory names a road the optimal route traverses, its window covers the trip, and the trace shows the vehicle leaving the corridor and rejoining. The cap is min(measured 2.98 km, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km) = 2.98 km, so the whole measured excess is exonerated. After that adjustment the excess remaining for POL-RD-01 is 0 km — below both gates — so no deviation survives and no POL-RD-02 recomputation of distance or time charges runs. The rider's distance and time lines stand, and the rider has properly conceded this.

Rider's ERP point — accepted. Your recovery is the tolls, and only the tolls. The optimal route carried no gantry at all (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00), yet you were billed $3.00 at the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry and $1.00 at the CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) gantry, both itemised as not on the optimal route. Because the detour is an external event exonerated under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-09(2) keeps the distance and time charges with the driver but returns off-route ERP to you as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at $12.00. That is $4.00 back, and the driver correctly accepts it is the ceiling of your recovery as well as the floor.

Rider's alternative arithmetic — declined. If the closure had only partly excused the detour, your POL-RD-02 working (charged_total 25.12 against a recomputed fare of 20.99, a difference of $4.15) would have been the right calculation. But the excess is fully exonerated, there is no excess left for POL-RD-02 to refund, so that $4.15 does not arise. The $4.00 is the only sum moving, it is refunded once, and there is no POL-RD-02 figure on top of it into which it could be double-counted (POL-RD-09(1)).

Billing integrity and conduct. The gantries were genuinely crossed on the CTE — the driver announced the CTE routing in-app at 08:12:30, before reaching either gantry, and the rider acknowledged it — so this is a pass-through correction under POL-RD-09(2), not a phantom charge under POL-RD-09(4), and no billing-integrity referral is warranted. The detour was announced by the driver rather than instructed by the rider (the only instruction-shaped message is the driver's, and waypoint_hint is null), so POL-RD-04 is unavailable and POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP correction; neither does it generate any driver compensation. The deviation is not material (36.3% and 2.98 km are below the 50% and 8.0 km marks), and the driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 553, so no POL-RD-06 pattern is established and no conduct referral or uplift follows.

Outcome. The rider is refunded SGD 4.00; the balance of the fare stands; nothing is paid to the driver; no referral issues.
